    THE DETAILS

    A little clarity.

    Who is this for?

    Small agencies and operations teams that use agents or automated workers to pay contractors. Start with one approved milestone, such as a final video edit or a design handoff.

    What does NEAR actually do?

    The Rust contract stores each approved job’s recipient, amount and state. It locks a job before transferring funds and processes the result afterward. The browser currently demonstrates that workflow locally; it does not call the contract.

    Does this catch every duplicate invoice?

    No. Protection is tied to the same approved job ID. Approving the same work under another ID creates a separate payment. Check your work reference before approving; automatic invoice matching is not implemented.

    Can I cancel a payment?

    You can cancel an approved job before execution starts. Once processing begins, wait for its outcome. A completed payment cannot be reversed here. In the demo, cancellation returns sample funds to the owner.

    What happens if an agent loses its connection?

    Keep using the same job ID and check its status. Do not create a new approval just because a response is slow. The contract keeps pending jobs locked; only a confirmed transfer failure permits retry.

    Is this escrow or proof that work was delivered?

    No. You decide that the work is ready to be paid before approving. PayoutLatch does not judge quality, resolve disputes or guarantee delivery.

    Can judges open this private site?

    This preview is currently owner-private. A judge-facing release will need accessible sharing, or a reproducible public repository and a demo video as allowed by rule Q-012. Changing the website’s audience is separate from choosing testnet.

    04 — DEPLOYMENT

    Know your network.

    The website and the blockchain have different jobs. This site hosts the interface; a deployed NEAR contract will hold approved funds and enforce payment rules.

    Payment receipt

    From approval to receipt

    1. Approve a job. The owner chooses a unique milestone, recipient and amount.
    2. Request payment. An authorized agent can execute only those approved terms.
    3. Wait for confirmation. Pending payments stay locked. Only a confirmed failure permits retry.
    4. Keep the receipt. Paid job IDs cannot be reused.

    This browser uses a local simulation. The Rust NEAR contract is separate; live wallet integration and testnet deployment are still pending.

    A second approval with a different ID is a separate payment. This does not establish whether work was delivered or identify every duplicate invoice.
